A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IterComp. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original IterComp benchmark results, ablations, qualitative comparisons, and a 23-participant user study in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds seed-stability measurements, DPG-Bench and GenEval results, and a revised 41-participant user study.

M1.justification: The model gallery, three composition-aware reward models, training losses, iterative dataset expansion, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Using IterComp within RPG was already demonstrated in v1; its new benchmark evaluation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds two evaluation suites beyond v1's T2I-CompBench coverage: DPG-Bench evaluates global, entity, attribute, and relational composition, while GenEval explicitly tests single objects, two objects, counting, colors, positions, and color binding. Training-data coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: MIGC, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated qualitative comparator in v2 Figure 10. The new stability comparison evaluates SD1.5, SDXL, InstanceDiffusion, Diffusion-DPO, and FLUX against IterComp. Existing benchmark-table and user-study comparator sets are retained; the Diffusion-DPO/ImageReward comparison is relocated, not newly added.

E3.justification: The user study changes from 23 participants, 16 prompts per comparison, and 1,840 overall-compositionality votes to 41 participants, 25 prompts per comparison, and 20,500 votes across four criteria. v2 also introduces the additional benchmark metrics and a controlled stability comparison. Existing training settings and the 40-step inference-time protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a dedicated cross-seed stability analysis for compositionality and CLIP score in Appendix A.3. Appendix A.6 adds layout-based comparison cases examining realism, detail, and malformed objects, while A.7 adds further comparative examples. The original gallery-size and iteration ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no explicit repeated-seed uncertainty analysis. v2 Appendix A.3 reports means and variances using the same 50 seeds across six models for two metrics, with variance represented by bubble radius. This introduces substantive variability reporting, without establishing increased run counts for the retained tables.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial new results. Table 6 reports DPG-Bench averages of 81.17, 81.28, and 84.72 for IterComp, RPG, and RPG+IterComp; Table 7 reports GenEval overall scores of 0.675, 0.660, and 0.723. Stability findings, additional qualitative outputs, and replacement user-study results are also added. The redesigned survey does not support a same-setting comparison with v1's win rates.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, Theorem 1, the gradient decomposition, and their Appendix A.2 proofs are retained, including Equations 3–19. Pagination and equation placement change without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a composition-aware model preference dataset and iterative co-refinement of reward and diffusion models that improves compositional generation. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion remain unchanged; abstract wording changes do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing stability to iterative self-correction, discussing complementary strengths of RPG and IterComp, and identifying specific layout-model failures. These extend the existing interpretation without reframing the paper. The new suggestion that RPG excels in positioning conflicts with Table 7, which reports 0.30 for RPG versus 0.33 for IterComp.

D1.justification: The repository pointer, BLIP/MLP reward-model description, learning rates, batch sizes, diffusion timesteps, reward scaling, and four-A100 hardware specification are retained. Added survey and seed-analysis settings concern evaluation and statistics; no separate implementation or resource-access change is documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds the GenEval reference by Ghosh et al. and extends comparative discussion of RPG and MIGC. The related-work section and the central positioning against existing compositional-generation and diffusion-alignment approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 lightly edits the abstract and setup, updates the publication header, removes the acknowledgement, moves the alignment comparison into the main results, and reorganizes and expands the appendix. This is a limited restructuring rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark Tables 6–7, stability plots, and several qualitative comparison panels. The user-study display changes from stacked win/tie/loss bars to grouped bars for four criteria. Table 5 moves into the main text, while the original supplementary image grid is retained as Figure 13. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation of the existing claims. In v1, RPG-backbone generalization is supported by selected images; v2 tests it quantitatively on two additional benchmarks. Matched-seed variability analysis and an aspect-specific human study also address gaps in evidence about consistency and the targeted compositional abilities. The unsupported positioning interpretation and coarse variance display are local weaknesses, but do not outweigh these gains.
